top_signals.title: BI Survey: Budgetary Constraints for 2027 Travel
top_signals.summary:
Jody Lurie, Bloomberg Intelligence Credit Analyst, discussed her recent Bloomberg Survey covering budgetary constraints for 2027 travel. Lurie spoke with Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu.on her recent BI surveys.
US vacationers appear poised to spend more in 2027, but inflation is reshaping rather than curbing demand as higher core trip costs squeeze spending on extras, based on Bloomberg Intelligence's seventh US travel survey conducted Oct. 26-Nov. 4. About 71% believe they'll spend more, but only 45% would absorb higher-than-expected costs vs. 50% two years ago, while 53% cite inflation as a reason for bigger budgets. This shift favors midtier hotels and pressures airline and cruise upselling, while generative AI is a nearer-term threat to deal-hunting than booking for Expedia, Booking Holdings and Airbnb. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: AI Is Coming for Economists in the White House, Says Claudia Sahm
top_signals.summary:
Claudia Sahm, Chief Economist at New Century Advisors, joined Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu to discuss her latest column, "AI Is Coming for the Economists in the White House." 
The AI debate, which economists have been having for years in various contexts, has come for the profession itself. Jason Furman, chair of the Council of Economic Advisers under President Barack Obama and now a professor at Harvard, recently said that if he were running the CEA today, he would “somewhat regretfully and sadly” use current AI systems instead of hiring 20 actual human economists. The chair’s job, he added, is safe. (Source: Bloomberg)
